newsitem.title: UK: UK engineering stocks dip as ABN Hoare downgrades.
newsitem.headline: UK engineering stocks dip as ABN Hoare downgrades.

text.p: Shares in engineering companies dipped on Friday after brokerage house ABN AMRO Hoare Govett downgraded its forecasts by about 10 percent on currency considerations, dealers and analysts said.
"The loss of faith in the sector has been dramatic," said ABN analysts in a research note.

Analyst Sandy Morris said, "The market is anticipating a recession in UK manufacturing but not necessarily in the UK economy but we could just potentially be hit by a manufacturing recession and then by a normal slowing in demand in the UK economy as rates rise."

ABN is recommending a neutral stance on the sector with an "undervalued" view on BBA, up 1/2p to 354-1/2p, FKI, up 7p to 170p, Siebe, off 8p to 998-1/2p, TI, off a penny to 506-1/2p, and Vickers, down 1-1/2p to 179p.
ABN rates "overvalued" Glynwed, up 1p to 221-1/2p, McKechnie, up 1/2p to 391p, and Morgan Crucible, up 6p to 430-1/2p.
ABN analysts said they were drawing a line under loss of faith in the sector by factoring translation and estimated transaction impacts of exchange rate movements into forecasts.

"We believe that there is value emerging in the sector, but are not convinced that we are yet out of the danger area in terms of results or trading statements that could adversely impact sentiment," said the note.
